full_judgment: 8. Mr. Shaheed Alam, learned Advocate for the appellants, submits that the suit land was validly acquired for Railway in L.A. Declaration in 1882 for setting up Narayangonj-Mymenshing Rail Line and accordingly RS. Record has been prepared in the name of the Railway and as such no question of title and possession of the plaintiffs arise. He submits that the High Court Division erroneously made the Rule absolute without reversing the concurrent findings of the Courts below. He further submits that the R.S. Khatian was prepared upon holding physical survey in the field and the plaintiffs having not been found in physical possession in the suit plot and the same being situated at the heart of Narayangonj town/city and no objection having been filed under Rules 30 and 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1954 the plaintiffs' claim of title and possession, since in purchase in 1969, is nothing but a got up story rather a cock and bull story which both the Courts below categorically found to be without any legal basis. Hence, according to him, the High Court Division committed error of law in setting aside the concurrent findings of the Courts below. He lastly submits that the High Court Division illegally interfered with the concurrent findings of fact of the Courts below that `Duburunnessa failed to prove her title on the basis of "Mourashi Patta" from C.S. recorded owner Yasin Hazi' and as such when Duburunnessa's title is not proved all subsequent transfers from Duburunnessa is nullity and as such void. Hence he prayed for allowing the appeal.
